page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized seventh-generation instance powered by the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It is equipped with 1 dedicated x86_64 vCPU running on an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz across 1 physical core. The memory system consists of 8.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio typical of memory-heavy instance classes. The CPU architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 4 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance includes no attached local NVMe storage and no bundled GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 3029.48, placing it in the top 25% tier. Single-threaded data handling achieves average rates of 29.13 GB/sec in gzip compression and 13.73 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, due to its single physical core design, multi-threaded throughput and overall parallel execution remain constrained, resulting in lower scores on multi-core benchmarks, compile tests, and database workloads. Memory write bandwidth reaches 26.49 GB/sec uncached, while Redis SET operations record 2.65 million operations per second.

The r7a.medium offers a cost-efficient hardware profile for memory-intensive applications that do not require multi-core compute resources. Its dedicated CPU allocation guarantees stable baseline performance without shared-core CPU credit limitations. This instance is best suited for lightweight in-memory caching layers, small relational databases, single-threaded web serving, and small-scale language model inference generation.
